720	Well, Rabbis, there are many things in the Talmud, "the words of the Sages and their riddles," that cannot be measured
721	or understood.
722	But notice here that the Rav takes this to his own subject. He says, as we find in the words of our Sages, of blessed memory, Yevamot, page 16,
723	that they went round and round through the halachot until they reached the "tzarat habat,"
724	it turns out that all the halachot they discussed earlier were not the main point
725	of the intention, but only circuits and introductions in order to reach the "tzarat
726	habat," which is the intended point.
727	And this is the meaning of the Zohar, "searah be'igula."
728	And this is the aspect of "searah ukmah," and the Zohar also writes "searah ukmah," black hair.
729	The aspect of "I am black and comely."
730	Why?
731	Because the higher intellect is what is inside, that is Chochmah.
732	The lower intellect is the hairs and so on, that is the aspect of Malchut.
733	And Malchut is in essence called "searah ukmah," black
734	hair.
735	Because blackness gathers the rays and contracts them in order to see well.
736	What does this mean?
737	How does a person see?
738	Through the pupil of the eye.
739	The pupil is black.
740	It is called "bat ayin."
741	And this is in essence the contraction.
742	The pupil contracts and expands when it needs to see,
743	in order to see well, because the lower intellect is an aspect of blackness that contracts in it the beauty and splendor of the higher intellect.
744	And these hairs are the aspect of "shiurah de'atvan de'Oraita," that is, the measure of the letters of the Torah.
745	Because the mitzvot are the wisdom of the Creator, may His Name be blessed. The mitzvot are, so to speak, the higher wisdom.
746	The mitzvot, but how can I define them, know them, understand them,
747	through Malchut? What is Malchut here?
748	The letters of the Torah.
749	The letters of the Torah.
750	For the mitzvot are the wisdom of the Creator, may His Name be blessed, for each and every mitzvah has other measures and limits, such as:
751	why is this mitzvah commanded this way? Because that is how His wisdom, may His Name be blessed, decreed. And another mitzvah is commanded
752	that way according to His wisdom, may His Name be blessed. And each and every mitzvah has letters, words, and matters that are
753	measures and limits in which His wisdom, may His Name be blessed, is contracted, which is the aspect of
754	the clothing of the higher intellect in the lower intellect, through which one merits divine perceptions, as mentioned above,
755	through the letters of the Torah.
756	Rabbenu the Ari writes that in the introduction of...
757	when a Torah scroll is lifted, one should draw close until he can see the letters of the Torah scroll, and through this a great awakening
758	will be drawn to him.
759	The language of Rabbenu the Ari in the other kavanot, in the discourses on the Torah scroll.
760	The splendor of that person.
761	"The splendor of that person" is an addition of later authors.
762	Rabbenu the Ari did not write it that way.
763	Maran Ben Yisraeli wrote this in another book, Le'Tiferet.
764	Ya bye, ya bye, ya bye, ya bye, ya bye. And this is the aspect of "Bat hayta le'Avraham
765	Avinu."
766	"Uvechol shamah."
767	So first of all, Rabbis, Avraham Avinu is an aspect of Chochmah.
768	Avraham is Chesed.
769	But we say Avraham Avinu, right?
770	Which is an aspect of what sefirah is above Chesed?
771	Chochmah.
772	Yes, I erred.
773	Chochmah.
774	"Uvechol shamah."
775	"Bat hayta le'Avraham Avinu uvechol."
776	"Bat" is the aspect of "bat ayin."
777	That is, the black of the eye, which is the aspect of the blackness mentioned above,
778	which contracts and limits, yes, which contracts and limits and includes
779	within itself all the great things standing before it.
780	For example, a great mountain, when it stands before the "bat ayin," which is the black of the eye,
781	then we receive the whole mountain within the "bat ayin" that sees it.
782	So we see in essence an example of how the higher intellect is contracted in the lower intellect.
783	Here the Rav says that the pupil...
784	Yes?
785	Do you know why the pupil is called "ishon"?
786	"Ish katan."
787	"Ish katan," a little man.
788	What does "little man" mean?
789	What is it?
790	It means that if now, even if someone big stands in front of you,
791	right?
792	188 kilos.
793	Big.
794	But in your pupil, you see him this small.
795	That is, everything, even a great mountain, is seen in the pupil.
796	Because the blackness in them contracts all the great things, and they are included and seen within it, and through this one sees and grasps
797	the thing that is seen.
798	Likewise, the lower intellect contracts and receives the great higher intellect and it is included within it, and through this
799	one sees, understands, and grasps the great higher intellect, as above. And this is the aspect of "And HaShem appeared to him in a flame of fire."
800	"Labat" of fire.
801	What does "in a flame of fire" mean? That HaShem, may He be blessed, wanted to clothe for him divine perceptions,
802	and it is impossible to grasp the higher intellect, for divine perceptions, without clothing in parables and many contractions.
803	And He clothed it for him in the aspect of the "bat ayin" mentioned above.
804	So this is the meaning of "And HaShem appeared to him in a flame."
805	So the "bat" refers to the meaning of the "bat ayin."
806	And this is the aspect of "bat techila siman yafe labanim."
807	"Bat techila" is the aspect of the lower intellect, through which one can reach the higher intellect,
808	which is a beginning and introduction to the higher intellect.
809	And this is the aspect of "a good sign for sons."
810	"Banim" is the aspect of the higher intellect, for the statement of our Sages, of blessed memory, in Menachot 110: "I will bring My sons
811	from afar and My daughters from the end of the earth."
812	"My sons from afar" are the exiles of Bavel, whose minds are settled like sons, which is the aspect of Chochmah.
813	Yes, I, the humble one, add that Rabbenu the Ari always writes that the word "rachok" (far) is
814	one of the names of Chochmah.
815	How do I know?
816	It is written, "And his sister stood afar off."
817	And what is written?
818	"Say to wisdom, You are my sister."
819	This is in many rivers.
820	So what is written here?
821	"I will bring My sons from afar," which is Chochmah, which is the higher intellect.
822	This is exactly what the Rav expounds here, only he brings an additional source for it.
823	"My sons from afar" are those exiles whose minds are settled like sons, as opposed to those exiles in other lands whose minds
824	are not settled, like daughters.
825	It turns out that "banim" are an aspect of settled mind, the aspect of the great higher intellect mentioned above, which one grasps through
826	introductions, the aspect of the lower intellect as above. And this is "bat techila," which is the lower intellect, "siman yafe labanim," through which
827	one grasps the higher intellect, which is the aspect of "banim," as above, and this is "a good sign."
828	Why is it a good sign?
829	Because "bat techila" is a sign, that is the limitation, that is the "bat ayin," that is
830	Malchut, that is "searah," measure.
831	And this is a good sign, in which the higher intellect is marked and limited in the aspect of "shiurah de'atvan de'Oraita."
832	"Shiurah," the measure of the letters of the Torah.
833	The aspect of "I am black and comely" is mentioned here.
834	That is all, Rabbis. With the help of HaShem we are blessed for today, and if HaShem wills we will continue in another
835	class, the next one.
836	Blessed is HaShem forever, amen and amen.
